scope: Bounded local model two-pass single-card review; not independent human approval.

cards.title: Consensus Means Me
cards.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You nodded at Friday. I'll announce unanimous support for my plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to Friday, not the plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. We've approved the timetable of my leadership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I object to the budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll announce unanimous calendar support first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You nodded at Friday. I'll tell the committee you've accepted me as project lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only agreed to the meeting date.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Everyone's following the timetable I set.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll attend, but I'm voting against your budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll introduce you as my finance watchdog. It's good to have the whole committee behind my leadership.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 claims approval of 'my leadership,' but A5 retreats to calendar support instead of treating it as acceptance of leadership.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's Friday distinction; A5 avoids B4's budget objection by returning to the calendar.

relationship.evidence: B2 limits consent and B4 objects to spending, but neither establishes B's practical stake in the announcement.

heightening.evidence: After B4 objects to the budget, A5 reduces the claim to 'calendar support' rather than increasing leadership entitlement.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies Friday and a planned announcement, but 'my plan' leaves the shared undertaking indistinct.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'timetable of my leadership' is compact but sounds more composed than sincerely managerial.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 converts agreement on Friday into acceptance of leadership; A5 converts attendance despite opposition into committee backing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 limits agreement to the date, which A3 calls following A's timetable; B4's budget opposition becomes A5's finance-watchdog appointment.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects A's claim and B4 preserves an opposing vote while agreeing to attend, giving B a credible committee position.

heightening.evidence: A5 goes beyond A1's claimed endorsement by assigning the budget opponent an office within A's presumed leadership.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies Friday, a committee and a project-lead claim; B4 adds a concrete budget dispute, though the project remains unspecified.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's timetable argument is economical; A5's 'finance watchdog' earns the turn, although its final sentence restates the premise.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2's meeting-date correction supplies the timetable that A3 treats as evidence of following A.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 agrees to attend but opposes the budget; A5 assimilates both into a finance role under A.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 consistently treat narrow cooperation as universal acceptance of A's leadership.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 incorporates an explicit opponent into A's administration, extending the initial misreading of a nod.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D71 converts limited agreement into evidence that everyone accepts A's leadership.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: This can resemble exaggerating support for a proposal, which need not imply personal leadership.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A3 names leadership, but original A5 only claims calendar support; revised A5 converts attendance into a position within A's administration.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the retreat at original A5 and clarified the committee setting. Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, A3/A5 convert limited cooperation into leadership; logic 5, B2 supplies the timetable and B4 supplies attendance plus financial opposition; relationship 4, B4 protects a vote; heightening 5, A5 appoints the objector; specificity 4, A1 establishes the committee project; brevity/wit 4, A5's watchdog appointment earns its turn. Total 93.
records.remainingConcern: A5's final claim of whole-committee support explains a joke already conveyed by the appointment. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A5's claim about the whole committee deliberately outruns evidence from one member; performance must keep that inference sincere.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a absorbs resistance through an assigned oversight role; b appropriates a cooperative proposal as delegated authority.

cards.title: Consensus Means Me
cards.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You like the blue poster? Good, the campaign has consensus.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I dislike the slogan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But its surroundings have your confidence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't say I endorse it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll say you helped establish the visual direction under me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You like the blue campaign poster? I'll tell the volunteers they're happy with me in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The colour, yes. Could we work on the slogan together?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm glad everyone's accepted my collaborative leadership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's each write one and let the volunteers choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. My first act as campaign leader is to delegate the decision.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims campaign consensus and A3 visual confidence; personal leadership appears only in A5's trailing 'under me.'

responseLogic.evidence: A3 evades B2's slogan objection through its surroundings; A5 adjusts the endorsement language after B4 forbids endorsement.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 protect B from misrepresentation, but B has no further campaign responsibility or alternative offer.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds 'under me' after B4's refusal, but mainly repackages the original claim.

specificity.evidence: A1's blue campaign poster and B2's disliked slogan provide concrete, playable points of disagreement.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's confidence in the slogan's 'surroundings' economically exploits B2's narrow objection.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats approval of blue as leadership endorsement; A3 treats joint slogan work as acceptance of 'my collaborative leadership.'

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's request to collaborate; A5 recasts B4's volunteer vote as A's delegation, though it drops the proposed competing slogans.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants joint authorship and B4 gives volunteers the choice; these offers establish a credible collaborator seeking shared control.

heightening.evidence: B4 distributes decision-making, and A5 claims the distribution itself as a first executive act.

specificity.evidence: A1's campaign poster and B2's slogan establish an immediately playable design conversation, without identifying the campaign.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'delegate the decision' neatly appropriates B4's democratic suggestion; A3 states the leadership premise rather explicitly.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 requests shared slogan work; A3 claims that request confirms A's collaborative leadership.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 proposes a volunteer decision; A5 calls that decision-making power a delegation from A.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A extrapolates from one person's limited agreement to acceptance of leadership by all volunteers.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 turns the proposal to share authority into an exercise of A's presumed authority.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D71 turns agreement with one campaign detail into confirmation of A's authority over the group.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Ordinary credit stealing would claim authorship of the poster or slogan without inferring acceptance of leadership.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 interprets B2's collaborative offer as acceptance of leadership, and A5 treats B4's shared vote as A's delegation.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised because original A1/A3 pursued proposal endorsement more clearly than leadership. Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, A1/A3/A5 repeatedly infer authority; logic 5, collaboration becomes leadership and voting becomes delegation; relationship 4, B2/B4 seek shared authorship and choice; heightening 4, A5 claims executive power over the vote; specificity 5, A1/B2 establish a campaign poster task; brevity/wit 4, A5's delegation follows B4 exactly. Total 92.
records.remainingConcern: A5 uses the volunteer vote more fully than the competing-slogan proposal. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The volunteers remain offstage, so A's assumption of their agreement must read as A's expansive inference.
records.alternativeComparison: Unlike a's resistant committee member, B here offers cooperation; A captures that cooperation through the language of collaboration and delegation.

cards.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
cards.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The kitchen supplies my team's tea. I need a kitchen key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You manage accounts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts require alertness. Tea controls alertness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where does that end?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The roof leaks on the kettle. I'll need that key too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts keeps missing tea because the kitchen's locked. I need control of the keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's a key. But the cleaners keep locking the kettle in their cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll approve their cleaning checklist. The kettle stays out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their contractor only takes instructions from the building manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the building manager's instructions need my approval. Otherwise accounts can't reliably have tea.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims kitchen access through the team's tea; A5 uses a roof leak to claim another key.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 links B2's accounts role to tea, but A5 introduces the roof leak after B4's generic 'Where does that end?'

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges A's remit, while B4 supplies a rhetorical question rather than a consequential operational response.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands from kitchen to roof, though B4 has not supplied the new problem driving that expansion.

specificity.evidence: A1's kitchen key and A3's accounts staff needing alertness make the workplace demand easy to play.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's short chain from accounts to alertness to tea gives A's overreach an economical rationale.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims control of keys; A3 claims approval of cleaning checklists; A5 claims approval of the building manager's instructions. Each new problem expands A's claimed jurisdiction.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 identifies cleaners locking away the kettle, prompting A3 to control their checklist. B4 identifies the manager as their authority, prompting A5 to control that authority.

relationship.evidence: B2 helps by providing a key and B4 explains the contractor's reporting constraint. B credibly facilitates access, although B's own role remains unspecified.

heightening.evidence: B4 makes checklist approval insufficient; A5 consequently demands oversight of the building manager while retaining A1's modest justification of tea for accounts.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a locked workplace kitchen; B2 adds the kettle cupboard. The objects are immediately playable, though authority over keys is only implied.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's checklist demand is economical, and A5 earns its disproportionate managerial claim through the continuing need for reliable tea.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2's cleaners control access to the kettle, so A3 seeks control of their cleaning checklist.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 locates effective authority with the building manager, so A5 places that manager's instructions under A's approval.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 turn successive access problems into entitlements to broader control.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 moves from controlling a kitchen procedure to supervising managerial instructions without abandoning the tea problem.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D72 uses each newly encountered obstacle to justify control over an additional area.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Seeking enough access to solve a problem would stop once B supplies a working key.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised B2 grants access but reveals the locked-away kettle; A3 claims the cleaning checklist, and A5 claims approval over the building manager's instructions after B4 identifies the contractor's reporting restriction.

records.recommendedEdit: Corrected the rejected candidate's unsupported keyholder concern while preserving the office setting and original firstPass. Separate internal re-read under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, A3/A5 claim authority over successive areas; logic 5, B2's inaccessible kettle causes checklist control and B4's reporting restriction causes managerial oversight; relationship 4, B2 helps with access while B4 explains a limit on implementing A's demand; heightening 4, A5 places the building manager's instructions under accounts; specificity 5, A1's locked kitchen and B2's kettle give immediate practical stakes; brevity/wit 4, A5's tea justification sustains the disproportionate claim. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns and causal hard gates pass; this is an internal re-read, not live testing.
records.remainingConcern: B's institutional role is underdefined, and the sequence is deliberately neat. Neither materially breaks the exchange. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A3 deliberately demands the whole checklist to solve one storage problem. A5's broader approval claim must remain sincerely grounded in reliable tea access.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved alternative pursues scheduling control outward toward council road closures. This candidate follows an internal chain of authority, with B initially helping by supplying a key.

cards.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
cards.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your delivery delays affect my schedule. I'll oversee transport.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You only book meeting rooms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: People travel to rooms. It's one system.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you manage the roads next?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the ones leading to my rooms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your deliveries keep arriving during meetings. I need to approve the van schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You book the rooms. I'll send you our arrival times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send the routes too. I'll approve those so the times hold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The council keeps closing the access road. We can't schedule around that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give them my number. Road closures will need to fit my room bookings.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 uses delivery delays to claim transport oversight, and A5 extends the claim to roads serving the rooms.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's meeting-room remit; A5 accepts the road expansion explicitly offered by B4.

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges scope, but B4's 'roads next?' chiefly supplies A with the final escalation.

heightening.evidence: A5 claims roads, but B4 supplies no new road problem requiring A to invent that claim.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes delivery delays and B2 identifies A as the meeting-room booker.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Only the ones leading to my rooms' makes an enormous claim sound carefully limited.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands van-schedule approval, A3 adds routes, and A5 claims influence over council closures in response to each scheduling obstacle.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 treats B2's arrival times as needing route control; B4's access-road closures specifically cause A5's demand to contact the council.

relationship.evidence: B2 identifies A's actual room-booking remit and offers information; B4 names a genuine limit on the delivery team's control.

heightening.evidence: B4 introduces municipal road closures, and A5 extends a room booker's presumed authority to the council.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes deliveries interrupting meetings and B2 establishes A's role; the venue and delivery relationship remain broad.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'fit my room bookings' makes the disproportionate claim legible without a separate joke, though A3's route rationale is compressed.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 offers arrival times; A3 demands the routes determining whether those times can hold.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 identifies council closures as the uncontrollable variable; A5 claims the council must accommodate A.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: Each new obstacle becomes grounds for A to control another layer beyond room bookings.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 escalates from coordinating deliveries to subordinating public road decisions to meeting arrangements.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D72 treats operational difficulties as warrants for extending A's decision-making jurisdiction.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Overenthusiastic coordination could request information while leaving other people's authority intact.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 insists on approving routes, and A5 makes council closures answerable to room bookings rather than merely requesting updates.

records.recommendedEdit: Replaced B4's suggested punchline with a concrete road-closure obstacle. Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, A3/A5 claim successive approval powers; logic 5, arrival times prompt route control and closures prompt council control; relationship 4, B2 offers information and B4 identifies a real limit; heightening 5, A5 subordinates council decisions; specificity 4, meetings, vans and access roads establish the work; brevity/wit 4, A5 keeps the absurd reach tied to bookings. Total 93.
records.remainingConcern: The move from supplied arrival times to route approval is plausible character logic but lightly motivated. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The council claim is a substantial comic leap, but it follows the newly supplied obstacle and A's established entitlement.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b turns operational coordination into a municipal demand; a stays within workplace keys and facilities.

cards.title: Be There for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come help me paint the old kitchen. I want you there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could hire someone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They wouldn't know why we're keeping that pencil mark.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm terrible at painting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll be terrible beside the mark together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come paint the old kitchen with me. Since Dad died, I barely see you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay someone. I can't face painting over his height marks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll keep them. Come help me tape around them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probably just sit on the floor and cry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll sit with you. We can leave the paint unopened; I don't want us only meeting to empty his house.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 rejects interchangeable hired help through the shared pencil mark; A5 values being together despite poor painting.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's hiring solution with shared history, and A5 directly accommodates B4's lack of painting skill.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a practical substitute and B4 admits inadequacy, making A explain why this particular person matters.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts a worse practical result after B4's admission, increasing commitment to companionship over competent help.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes painting an old kitchen, and A3's preserved pencil mark gives the shared history a playable object.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's being 'terrible beside the mark together' turns B4's objection into a tender, economical invitation.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 connects painting together to barely seeing B since Dad died. A5 explicitly abandons the paint while continuing to seek a relationship beyond emptying the house.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 fears losing Dad's height marks; A3 proposes taping around them. B4 anticipates crying rather than working; A5 offers to sit together with the paint unopened.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers payment while revealing grief, and B4 admits limited emotional capacity. A3 and A5 accommodate both concerns while preserving the request for connection.

heightening.evidence: B4 prompts A5 to relinquish productive work entirely and commit to shared grief. The development deepens the emotional request rather than increasing comic pressure.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes the old kitchen and bereavement; B2's height marks and A3's protective tape give the relationship a concrete, playable focus.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'tape around them' expresses care economically. A5's unopened paint earns the emotional turn, although its final explanation is more explicit than witty.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2's specific fear of painting over the height marks produces A3's invitation to preserve them together.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 says participation may consist only of crying; A5 accepts that form of presence and removes the obligation to paint.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1 and A5 make B's presence evidence that the connection survives beyond the practical work of clearing Dad's house.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 gives up the original task to secure the more vulnerable form of involvement B4 makes available.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D73 makes this person's participation evidence that a shared connection continues to matter.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Recruiting useful help would favor the competent painter that B2 proposes.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A1 identifies lost contact after Dad's death; A3 protects the marks that trouble B2, and A5 relinquishes painting to secure time together after B4 anticipates grief.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected original's thin partner position and repeated final invitation. Added bereavement and clearing Dad's house as illustrative context. Separate internal re-read under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, A1/A5 make continued contact the purpose of help; logic 5, B2's threatened marks cause A3's protective task and B4's anticipated crying causes A5 to give up painting; relationship 4, B2 offers money while B4 reveals the emotional barrier; heightening 4, A5 sacrifices the task to ask for a connection beyond estate chores; specificity 5, A1's kitchen and B2's height marks locate the encounter; brevity/wit 4, A5's unopened paint concretely expresses the changed priority without a separate joke. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns and causal hard gates pass on internal re-read.
records.remainingConcern: The scene offers emotional clarity rather than a substantial comic turn, and A5 states its meaning explicitly. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The bereavement makes this a tender example with little overt comedy. A5 proposes time together without assuming that B is ready to enter the house.
records.alternativeComparison: This alternative seeks continuing sibling connection through shared grief and relinquishes the task. D73-single-b seeks a father's presence at a milestone and offers a private occasion to avoid divorce-related pressure.

cards.title: Be There for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you come to my opening? Even for ten minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know anything about sculpture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You know me. That's the qualification.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I might say the wrong thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say it in person. That's the bit I'm asking for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, will you come to my opening? Even for ten minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know anything about sculpture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You survived every school play. I still want you in my corner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your mother will be there. We haven't spoken since the divorce.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come before we open. I'll unpack the biggest piece with you. I want a memory of tonight with you in it too.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 makes knowing A the qualification for attending, and A5 asks for personal presence even with an unsuitable comment.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's lack of sculpture knowledge; A5 directly repurposes B4's fear of saying the wrong thing.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 express credible anxiety about attending an art opening, requiring A to lower the social demands.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves beyond waiving expertise to welcoming the feared mistake, provided B actually comes.

specificity.evidence: A1's opening and ten-minute request combine with B2's sculpture reference to establish a playable invitation.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Say it in person' economically converts B4's exact objection into the desired commitment.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 requests Dad's attendance, A3 says 'I still want you in my corner,' and A5 seeks a memory containing him. Presence consistently signifies the relationship.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's lack of sculpture knowledge by invoking school-play attendance. A5 answers B4's divorce concern with a pre-opening visit, though Mum's absence then is assumed.

relationship.evidence: B2 presents discomfort about art, then B4 reveals the more consequential obstacle of encountering an estranged spouse. A5 changes the invitation to accommodate Dad.

heightening.evidence: B4 prompts A5 to replace brief public attendance with helping unpack the biggest piece, giving Dad a personal role in the opening.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies Dad and an opening; B2 establishes sculpture, and A5 provides an unpacking task. The venue and pre-opening access remain lightly sketched.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'survived every school play' supplies affectionate wit linked to B2's objection. A5's memory request is earned but somewhat polished.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 treats artistic knowledge as a prerequisite; A3 uses their school-play history to establish that parental support is enough.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 reveals the prospect of meeting Mum after the divorce; A5 offers a separate visit before public opening and a shared task.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A3 and A5 explain why this particular person's presence matters beyond attendance numbers or practical help.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 develops the request for ten minutes into a meaningful shared memory through active involvement.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D73 seeks attendance from a personally significant person as an expression of the connection.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Seeking praise for artistic work would require a favorable response rather than merely showing up.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 makes the father's history of attending school plays the relevant qualification; A5 arranges a separate shared moment after B4 reveals why ordinary attendance is difficult.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected original's repeated reassurance by giving B a distinct family obstacle and A a consequential accommodation. Added a father and divorced parents as illustrative context. Separate internal re-read under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, A3/A5 seek evidence of continuing parental involvement; logic 5, B2's expertise concern prompts A3's attendance history and B4's divorce prompts A5's earlier visit; relationship 4, B4 supplies a credible reluctance that A accommodates; heightening 4, A5 turns ten-minute attendance into a specific shared contribution and remembered moment; specificity 5, A1's opening and A5's unpacking offer an immediate activity; brevity/wit 4, A3's school-play comparison earns its gentle humor from B2. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns and causal hard gates pass on internal re-read.
records.remainingConcern: Coming before opening plausibly avoids Mum but does not explicitly guarantee it. A5's final sentence is slightly composed. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: An early visit may not remove every difficulty created by the divorce. A5 offers a workable opening for B's response rather than claiming the family tension is resolved.
records.alternativeComparison: D73-single-a removes practical expectations to permit shared grief. This alternative creates a practical role and changes timing to obtain parental involvement despite estrangement between the parents.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishes are done. Before you go, are we actually okay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The kitchen's spotless.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking about the people who cleaned it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What else needs doing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sentence that lets me put my coat on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishes are done. Before you go, are we actually okay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed to clean up. I've done that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Could you stay for the part that isn't the kitchen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got ten minutes before the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit with me for nine. I don't want the last thing we fixed tonight to be the sink.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 delays B's departure for relational repair, but A5 shifts to what will let A put a coat on.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 distinguishes people from B2's spotless kitchen; A5 answers B4's task question with a requested sentence.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 evade emotional discussion through completed cleaning and remaining chores.

heightening.evidence: A5 specifies a sentence but does not sharpen the cost of keeping B present, and changes whose departure is foregrounded.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes finished dishes and imminent departure; B2 keeps the kitchen situation concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'people who cleaned it' efficiently redirects B2's practical answer toward the relationship.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 explicitly separates completed dishes from an unrepaired relationship; A3 asks B to remain for the emotional work.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 acknowledges B2's completed cleanup; A5 uses B4's ten-minute bus limit to request precisely nine minutes.

relationship.evidence: B2 limits the commitment to cleaning and B4 needs the last bus; A5 accommodates that need while pursuing repair.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns a general request to stay into a bounded, urgent attempt at repair before the bus deadline.

specificity.evidence: A1's finished dishes and B4's last bus make both the practical release and remaining emotional urgency immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'part that isn't the kitchen' is concise; A5's sink callback is earned, though slightly polished for ordinary speech.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 says the agreed practical task is complete; A3 acknowledges this and asks for a different reason to stay.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 supplies ten minutes until the last bus; A5 bargains for nine rather than ignoring departure.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: The scene explicitly continues the effort to keep B present after the cleanup justification disappears.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 makes emotional repair time-limited and personally important while leaving B free to respond.
